title: Deposit to departure: how yacht catering bookings are confirmed
body_markdown:
Instead of chasing separate messages about the menu, deposit and boarding time, keep your yacht catering booking confirmation in one written record. Before treating arrangements as settled, ask the caterer to acknowledge the agreed service, payment status and boarding details; then share the same version with your yacht contact so food preparation and vessel access follow one plan.


**TL;DR**

- For myCHEF yacht catering enquiries, request written confirmation of the menu, payment status, staffing and boarding arrangements.
- A deposit receipt records payment; ask separately whether the catering booking is confirmed.
- Keep yacht catering booking confirmation separate from vessel arrangements and departure approval.
- Agree how guest-count, menu and departure changes will be acknowledged before preparation begins.


## Why the confirmation matters

A receipt answers whether a payment was received. It does not, by itself, explain which menu version applies, who meets the catering team or what happens if departure changes. **Ask for a booking acknowledgement that connects the payment to the agreed scope.**

myCHEF provides yacht catering and onboard chef services, not yacht hire or charter. For a catering enquiry, use the [contact page](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) to send your date, boarding location, guest count and requested service. Make clear whether you need food delivered or a chef working onboard.

**myCHEF yacht catering is for hosts who need food or an onboard chef, rather than a vessel booking.** This guide explains what to request and check; the written terms supplied for your event determine its payment, amendment and cancellation conditions.

## Before you start

- **Gather the event brief.** Have the date, guest count, dietary requirements, preferred menu style and intended service format ready. Separate confirmed details from decisions still open.
- **Identify the decision-makers.** Name the person approving catering, the person paying and the yacht contact responsible for boarding access. Obtain the latest proposal and any payment instructions already supplied.
- **Check the boarding window, not just departure.** Ask your yacht contact when the catering team can board, where supplies enter and which equipment can be used. A departure time alone does not give the team an agreed setup window.

Keep these details in a shared document or a clearly identified email thread. The headings below are suggested headings for that record, not fields in a particular booking system.

## Event brief and service scope

### Establish what the catering booking covers

1. **Write an Event brief.** Record the event date, yacht identifier, marina, boarding point, guest count and lead contact. Mark any unconfirmed location or timing clearly rather than allowing an assumption to become an instruction.
2. **Select the Service format.** State whether you want delivered food, onboard preparation or staffed service. Ask the caterer which arrangements are suitable for the vessel and proposed menu before choosing.
3. **Record Menu and dietary requirements.** List dishes, serving style and individual dietary needs. Distinguish an allergy from a preference, and ask the caterer to confirm what can be accommodated.
4. **Agree Inclusions and exclusions.** Ask who supplies crockery, cutlery, serving equipment, drinks, ice, staff and waste removal. Record only the items expressly included in your proposal.

**Expected result:** the host and caterer have the same written definition of the service. The yacht contact can then check the plan against the actual space and facilities onboard.

### Compare formats before approving the scope

These are planning formats, not a statement that every option is included in a particular package. Ask which format the caterer can provide for your event.

| Format | Best for | Practical advantage | Limitation to resolve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivered catering | Hosts who want food handed over before departure | Does not require a chef to remain onboard | Allocate responsibility for storage, serving and clearing |
| Onboard chef | Hosts who want dishes prepared or finished onboard | Allows preparation to be coordinated with service | Confirm workspace, equipment, boarding and disembarkation |
| Staffed catering | Hosts who want help serving guests | Gives serving tasks a named owner | Define staff duties, working period and clearing scope |

Do not choose the format from the menu photographs alone. A dish that looks appropriate still needs an agreed preparation, storage and service arrangement. Send the yacht contact the proposed format before approving it.

## Proposal approval and deposit acknowledgement

### Connect the payment to the correct proposal

1. **Review the Proposal.** Check the event date, guest count, menu version, service format and named inclusions. Ask for corrections before approving; do not rely on an earlier message to override an inaccurate document.
2. **Read the Payment terms.** Confirm the deposit requirement, payment deadline, balance deadline and cancellation conditions in the supplied terms. Ask how a date change, vessel change or reduced guest count affects the agreement.
3. **Follow the supplied payment instructions.** Use the payment reference requested by the caterer. If payment details change unexpectedly, verify them through an established contact before sending funds.
4. **Request a Booking acknowledgement.** Ask the caterer to acknowledge receipt, identify the proposal it relates to and state the booking status. Keep the receipt alongside that acknowledgement.

**Expected result:** you have written evidence of both payment and the catering arrangement it supports. Any remaining conditions are explicit rather than buried in a conversation.

### What should the acknowledgement say?

Request a concise summary that identifies:

- The event date and booking contact.
- The approved proposal or menu version.
- The guest count and service format.
- The payment received and any remaining payment deadline.
- Any outstanding decisions, with an owner and agreed deadline.
- The terms that apply to changes or cancellation.

**Do not treat an unanswered payment screenshot as a completed confirmation.** Ask for acknowledgement and a clear statement of what remains outstanding. This is a verification step, not a claim that every caterer uses the same booking process.

## Boarding plan and final event handover

### Turn the confirmed scope into arrival instructions

1. **Create a Boarding plan.** Ask the yacht contact for the precise meeting point, access contact and permitted loading arrangements. Share the catering team's requirements for carrying supplies and equipment onboard.
2. **Separate the event times.** Record catering arrival, guest boarding, departure, intended food service and staff disembarkation where relevant. Ask each responsible party to acknowledge the times that affect them.
3. **Check the onboard facilities.** Confirm usable preparation space, refrigeration, water, power and cooking equipment with the yacht contact. Ask the caterer whether the agreed menu works with those facilities.
4. **Issue the Final handover.** Send the latest brief, menu, access instructions and contact details together. Identify unresolved points explicitly and request acknowledgement from the people responsible.

**Expected result:** the catering team knows where to arrive, what to bring and who will receive them. The yacht contact knows what the catering team needs before guests board.

Keep the handover sequence simple: **Event brief**, **Proposal approval**, **Payment acknowledgement**, **Boarding plan**, **Final handover**. Each stage should leave a written record that the next person can use without reconstructing the conversation.


![Booking handover stages from the event brief to the final catering instructions](https://media.get-ryze.ai/workspace-article-images-public/b761b9c9-f216-4026-8747-edf93062ff00/body-9799be21de882ac815d533de4964edff.jpg)

*Connect the approved catering scope to the boarding instructions before the event.*


Do not substitute a map pin for a named boarding contact. Ask who will answer the catering team's call and what to do if the vessel is not at the expected position. Keep those instructions in the same record as the arrival time.

## Change control when the plan moves

### Update a confirmed booking without losing the agreed version

1. **Send a Change request.** State the original detail, the requested replacement and the event it concerns. Keep the request specific: guest count, menu, service time, vessel or boarding point.
2. **Ask for an impact check.** Request confirmation of any effect on staffing, preparation, equipment, payment or access. A request is not an accepted amendment until the relevant parties acknowledge it.
3. **Approve the revised scope.** Keep the accepted revision together with any updated terms. Label the previous version as superseded so it is not reused accidentally.
4. **Redistribute the handover.** Send the accepted update to the host, caterer and yacht contact. Ask each person to confirm the details within their responsibility.

**Expected result:** everyone works from the same accepted revision. No one has to guess whether a later message replaced the original instruction.

### Illustrative guest-count change

Suppose your approved brief lists **12 guests** and a **2-course meal**. You then request catering for **16 guests**, while keeping the departure time unchanged. These figures are an example, not a myCHEF package or capacity statement.

Do not update the number alone. Ask the caterer to reassess food quantities, dietary portions, serving equipment and staffing, then ask the yacht contact to check the revised service arrangements. Record the accepted revision before treating the additional guests as catered for.

The same method applies to a changed boarding point. Obtain the new location, access contact and arrival instructions, then have the catering team acknowledge them. Forwarding a location message without acceptance leaves the handover incomplete.

## Troubleshooting confirmation problems

### The deposit is paid, but there is no booking acknowledgement

Send the payment reference through the established contact thread and ask for receipt confirmation. Request the event date, approved proposal and outstanding conditions in the reply. Avoid sending another payment simply because the first has not yet been acknowledged.

### The menu differs across messages

Ask the caterer to identify the version awaiting approval. Put subsequent amendments into that version and request a consolidated copy. **One accepted menu is clearer than several partially approved conversations.**

### The yacht contact cannot confirm the equipment

List the uncertain facilities and ask the caterer which menu items depend on them. Resolve the equipment question or revise the preparation method before approving that part of the plan. Do not describe equipment as usable because it appears in a photograph.

### Departure changes after catering is confirmed

Notify the caterer immediately and request an impact check. Confirm revised boarding, service and disembarkation arrangements with the yacht contact as well. A changed departure does not automatically establish a revised catering schedule or extend staff attendance.

### An allergy is added late

Contact the caterer directly and request an explicit response about whether it can be accommodated. Do not remove an ingredient from the written menu yourself and assume the preparation arrangements are suitable. Share the confirmed outcome with the affected guest or their responsible adult.

## Make the final handover useful

A useful handover is short enough to check at the boarding point. Keep the event summary at the top, followed by access instructions, menu, dietary requirements and responsibilities. Place receipts and longer terms behind that working summary rather than mixing them into arrival instructions.

Ask who owns each practical task: receiving delivered food, setting the table, serving drinks, clearing dishes and removing waste. For questions about those boundaries, the guide to [serving staff and cleanup](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup) provides a related starting point; your event proposal still determines the agreed scope.

Before departure, check unresolved items rather than reopening settled choices. Verify that the catering team has the accepted instructions and that the yacht contact knows whom to expect. Keep vessel decisions with the yacht operator and catering decisions with the caterer.

## FAQ


**What should a yacht catering booking confirmation include?**

A yacht catering booking confirmation should identify the date, guest count, approved menu, service format, payment status and agreed terms. Keep boarding instructions and outstanding decisions with the same record so the event can be handed over clearly.

**Does paying a deposit mean my yacht catering is confirmed?**

Ask the caterer to confirm the booking status in writing after acknowledging the deposit. A payment receipt records the transaction; the acknowledgement should connect it to the approved proposal and identify any remaining conditions.

**Can I change the guest count after confirming yacht catering?**

Request a written amendment and have the caterer confirm whether it can be accepted under your booking terms. Ask about effects on quantities, dietary portions, staffing, equipment and payment before treating the change as agreed.

**Who should confirm the catering team's boarding arrangements?**

Ask the yacht contact responsible for access to confirm boarding arrangements with the catering team. Record the meeting point, arrival time, loading instructions and contact person separately from guest boarding and departure.

**Does myCHEF arrange yacht hire as part of catering?**

myCHEF provides yacht catering and onboard chef services, not yacht hire or charter. Arrange the vessel separately and share its confirmed access details and facilities when discussing the catering brief.

**What happens if the departure time changes?**

Request an impact check from the caterer and revised access instructions from the yacht contact. Obtain acceptance of the updated catering schedule rather than assuming the original staffing and service arrangements automatically shift.

**Should dietary requirements be confirmed before paying a deposit?**

Confirm essential dietary requirements before approving the catering proposal. Ask the caterer to state what it can accommodate and include the accepted requirements in the booking record; do not assume a menu label answers an individual allergy question.

- [From a guest list to a plated dinner](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/guest-list-to-plated-dinner-private-chef-event-workflow)

## Send a brief that can be confirmed

The detail easiest to overlook is the gap between departure and catering access. **Confirm when the team can board, not only when the yacht leaves.** That gives the caterer a defined setup window to assess before accepting the plan.

For a myCHEF yacht catering enquiry, send your date, marina or boarding location, guest count and service required. Include dietary requirements, the yacht contact and any known facilities, then ask for a proposal with clear inclusions and written confirmation steps.
